question.text: SEBI mandates prompt continuous disclosure of price-sensitive information under LODR Regulations and requires UPSI protection under PIT Regulations. Which form of market efficiency do these disclosure regimes PROMOTE and which do they implicitly ACCEPT is violated?

answer.text: They promote weak-form efficiency and accept that strong-form is violated.
They promote semi-strong-form efficiency (by forcing price-sensitive info into the public domain) and implicitly accept that strong-form is violated (since insiders would otherwise exploit UPSI).
They promote strong-form efficiency and accept weak-form is violated.
They are unrelated to the EMH framework.

explanation.text: The Logic: LODR-style continuous-disclosure pushes price-sensitive information into the public domain so that all investors can trade on it - this is exactly the semi-strong-form condition. PIT Regulations exist because, absent controls, insiders would profit from UPSI, which is exactly what strong-form EMH would forbid. Thus disclosures promote semi-strong efficiency; PIT accepts strong-form is violated. The Trap: Option A misassigns weak-form (historical prices, no disclosure angle). Option C inverts. Option D dismisses the regulatory-EMH linkage that is textbook. Cross-Exam Context: III-A (compliance), XV (RA), XIX-A/B/C all touch this interplay. XIX-C expects the manager to articulate these links at IC / LP meetings. Manager's Pro-Tip: Your AIF's Code of Conduct, pre-clearance policy and UPSI register translate SEBI's semi-strong / strong-form assumptions into operating processes. Audit them annually - LPs increasingly request this as part of ODD.
